notes: DJI D-Log M drone clip, Nov 10 2026 17:11 (shot 9 minutes after the first drone clip): dusk. 0-14 s the last pink-orange alpenglow on a ridge, 15-29 s the drone pans across open pale sky, 30-45 s a dark forested slope with snow in shade. Own look from its hues: alpenglow (hue ~45-55) kept natural: no extra for it, reds/browns around 40 eased to x0.88 so the slopes don't turn red, vibrance 0.5 (the first try had the alpenglow at color 0.18, too orange; this one 0.11-0.13, like the approved gold) (the user found the first clip's peak too orange), sky a touch bluer, evergreens a bit richer; log footage, so the first clip's approved curve, saturation and vibrance. No people, so no skin guard. Sharpening low (dusk shadows are noisy). Camera exposure only drifts (-0.15 at most), so no time keys. | v2 (user: 'make the color pop... more vivid... cooler hue, blues bluer, greens greener, the warm colors can stay the same'): sky band 240 x1.9 with cyan-side sky turned 10 deg toward blue, and sky_deepen (bright near-white blue sky darkened up to 0.07 so it can hold blue: at 6 s and 39 s the sky was at the screen's limit and a chroma gain alone did nothing); greens band 135 x2.2 (dim pines, raw color ~0.01) with olive turned 10 deg greener; cyan 190 x1.5 to bridge; cool_tint b -0.013 on grays, snow, shade and sky, kept off warm AND green hues and off the dark (it turned dim pines teal, hue 126->155, in the first try). Warm stays exactly: gold identical per pixel, browns median unchanged. v1 is in git history.
